ConocoPhillips rose 0.58% today as oil prices climbed toward the $100 mark, with world crude hitting $96.02 per barrel. The driver was escalating U.S.-Iran tensions—over the past few days, the two countries traded military strikes, with reports of attacks on U.S. Navy ships and Saudi Aramco facilities. These geopolitical flareups typically trigger concern about potential disruptions to Middle East energy supplies, which supports crude prices and lifts the stock price of a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips.

The stock has gained 1.27% over two weeks as this tension has built. However, today's move was modest despite oil climbing sharply, which suggests the market may be pricing in uncertainty about whether these tensions will actually disrupt supply flows or remain contained.
